wiki.content: "Remember the Time" is a new jack swing track by Michael Jackson, released on January 14, 1992, as the second single from his eighth studio album, Dangerous. The song was written by Michael Jackson, Teddy Riley, and Bernard Belle, and produced by Jackson and Riley. It blends R&B, funk, and pop elements with the contemporary new jack swing sound that Teddy Riley helped pioneer. The song was both a commercial and critical success, reaching number three on the Billboard Hot 100 and topping the charts in several countries. The song lyrically reflects on a past romantic relationship, with Jackson reminiscing about better times and expressing a longing for the emotional connection that once was. Jackson’s vocal performance is both smooth and dynamic, blending falsetto with rhythmic phrasing that fits the track’s percussive groove. Teddy Riley’s production brought a modern edge to Jackson’s sound, aligning him with the musical trends of the early 1990s while still maintaining his distinctive artistic identity. The music video for "Remember the Time," directed by John Singleton, was a cinematic short film set in ancient Egypt. It featured appearances by Eddie Murphy, Iman, Magic Johnson, and model Tom "Tiny" Lister Jr., and was praised for its high production value and groundbreaking visuals. The video helped push the boundaries of music video storytelling and was notable for portraying Black royalty in a glamorous, mythical setting—something rarely seen in mainstream pop culture at the time. "Remember the Time" became one of the standout tracks of the Dangerous album and remains one of Jackson's most beloved singles. It exemplifies his ability to evolve artistically and collaborate with younger producers while still delivering timeless pop music. The song continues to be celebrated for its infectious rhythm, memorable hook, and innovative music video, solidifying its place in both Michael Jackson's discography and 1990s music history.
